stem: A rigid camera bracket is attached to the chassis without relative motion. Which model structure best follows the link/joint distinction?

Use a continuous joint solely because the robot as a whole can move
Use a revolute joint with changing angle solely because the camera observes a changing scene
Represent the rigid bodies as links connected by a fixed joint

citations.locator: Lecture 5, printed slide 32; Printed 32. URDF is XML for appearance, dimensions and kinematic structure. Rigid links have visual, collision and inertial properties. Joint examples are fixed camera mount, continuous wheel and revolute arm hinge. A model property alone is not a safety certificate.

stem: A detector reports an object in camera coordinates, but navigation needs chassis-relative coordinates. Which information supplies the required frame relationship?

options.text: The base-to-world pose alone, without any camera-to-base connection
The camera visual mesh alone, without a coordinate transform to base_link
A valid TF relation connecting camera_link to base_link at the relevant time
The camera intrinsic calibration alone, without its pose relative to the chassis

assumptions: The required frame relation is valid and available for the measurement time.

citations.locator: Lecture 5, printed slide 33; Printed 33. TF represents mathematical relations between coordinate frames in 3D. The tree example places camera_link below base_link; non-root frames have one parent and may have children. URDF is the blueprint, while TF supplies changing frame relations. The /tf topic distributes transforms. Exactness and availability require valid, timely transforms, not merely subscription.
